summary: Unpacks bit-packed elements from an input buffer into per-element byte fields written backwards, driven by a bit depth read from this+0x9 (1, 2 or 4 bits per element) and an element count from this+0x0. When the depth is >= 8 the function does nothing. After the unpack (or when the depth is another value below 8) it updates packing metadata: resets this+0x9 to 8, writes this+0xB = 8 * this+0xA and this+0x4 = element count * this+0xA. Called by sub_51389E.

operations.description: Read the bit depth v3 from this+0x9; when v3 >= 8 the function returns immediately and neither unpacks nor updates metadata
Load the element count v4 from this+0x0 (dword)

1-bit unpack path (v3 == 1): for each of the v4 elements extract (*(src) >> (7 - ((v4-1) & 7))) & 1 into the destination bytes written backwards from a2 + v4 - 1, advancing the source byte each time the shift wraps
2-bit unpack path (v3 == 2): for each of the v4 elements extract (*(src) >> (6 - 2*((v4-1) & 3))) & 3 into the destination bytes, advancing the source when the shift wraps
4-bit unpack path (v3 == 4): for each of the v4 elements extract (*(src) >> (4 - 4*((v4-1) & 1))) & 0xF into the destination bytes, advancing the source when the shift wraps
Other bit depths below 8 (and a zero element count) skip the unpack loops and fall through to the metadata update
Read the multiplier v16 from this+0xA (byte)
Write this+0x4 = v4 * v16 (element count times multiplier), the computed output size
